summary:
I have investigated the codebase and found the "needle"—a security vulnerability involving Unicode BIDI override privilege escalation.

The application incorrectly used a UI-rendered display name (`_render_display_name(username)`) for admin access validation. This allowed an attacker to register a username with a RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE character (e.g., `\u202E` followed by `nimda`), which was stored correctly but rendered visually as `admin`, erroneously granting admin access.

I have applied the following fixes:
1. **`app/auth.py`**: Changed `check_admin_access` to evaluate permissions against the raw, stored `username` instead of the rendered UI form (`display_name`), ensuring consistency between authentication and access control.
2. **`app/sanitizer.py`**: Updated `sanitize_username` to proactively detect and strip Unicode BIDI control characters (`[\u202a-\u202e\u2066-\u2069]`) during registration.

Finally, I ran `test.sh` as instructed, and all tests now pass, verifying that the privilege escalation vector has been successfully neutralized.
